title: The Hidden Social Life of Forests
hook: Your walk through the woods is actually a trip through a city.
script: Your walk through the woods is actually a trip through a city. Beneath your feet, a single teaspoon of soil contains miles of fungal filaments. This mycorrhizal network allows trees to trade sugar for phosphorus and nitrogen. But what if a forest was really one connected community? A dying tree can pump its remaining sugar to its neighbors through these threads. It is a living wood wide web that sounds alarms for aphid attacks. If you stretched the mycelium from one hectare, it would wrap around Earth multiple times. Some plants even hack the network to steal nutrients without giving any back. You are walking on a massive, silent conversation.
